host_cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E3-1245 V2 @ 3.40GHz (Ivy Bridge)
measurement_note: All 6 benchmarks live in research/agy/bend5k/unseen_oracle_w19/, are brand-new programs outside bench/runtime/* and native45, pass upstream locked_bun.sh --check-only, and produce bit-identical stdout checksums across Proven-18 bend5k_o2 -O2, gcc-10 -O2, and gcc-10 -O3 -march=native. Every Silicon Oracle probe redirects ONLY the target symbol(s) inside the unmodified Proven-18 bend5k_o2 -O2 ELF64 .o via SHT_SYMTAB SHN_UNDEF redirection to a hand-edited GAS .s / C-intrinsic patch object, linked against the unmodified runtime-agy.o, with 5-run medians on CPU 0 and exact checksum verification.

probes.benchmark: research/agy/bend5k/unseen_oracle_w19/u1_stencil2d.bend (64x64 F32 5-point Jacobi heat stencil, 4000 ping-pong steps)
probes.primary_mechanism: Proven-18 emits 917 lines / 85 spills / 87 jcc in $direct.stencil_row with 0 SIMD ops: (1) single-constructor record GPair{src, dst} carried across self-TCO loop is unboxed and re-boxed with p111_program/p111_cid_hot checks on EVERY pixel; (2) dst Array<F32> handle tag/shift/base is re-decoded on EVERY pixel instead of hoisted to preheader; (3) F32 values bounce through GP registers via movd and constants 0.5/0.125 are reloaded per cell; (4) scalar 1-wide execution over 64-bit array slots vs gcc-10 -O3 -march=native 8-wide AVX1.

variants.name: a_unboxed_hoisted_scalar_stencil_row
variants.note: 6.17x speedup (170.76ms -> 27.67ms, 1.173x vs gcc-10 -O2) purely from unboxing GPair{src,dst} loop-carry + hoisting both Array<F32> handles + XMM-resident scalar F32.

variants.name: b_sse41_4wide_64bit_slot_stencil_row
variants.note: 9.86x speedup (170.76ms -> 17.32ms, BEATS gcc-10 -O2 at 0.735x!) using 4-wide SSE (movups + shufps $0x88 pack / unpcklps+unpckhps scatter) over Bend's existing 64-bit slots with 0 ABI change.

variants.name: c_packed_f32_avx1_8wide_run_steps
variants.note: 15.67x speedup (170.76ms -> 10.90ms, 0.462x O2, 1.202x O3-native) via non-escaping packed float[4096] stack promotion (32 KB L1D-resident) + 8-wide AVX1 stencil.

probes.general_compiler_pass: Tier 1 (6.17x): Unbox single-constructor record parameters across self-TCO loops + extend Linear-Array Hoist (Law 4) to ALL arrays unpacked from loop-carried records (src + dst) + keep F32 SSA values in XMM registers. Tier 2 (9.86x-15.67x): 4-wide SSE strided F32 loop vectorization and non-escaping local Array<F32> packed float[N] promotion + 8-wide AVX1.
probes.verdict: STRONG GO (6.17x from Tier 1 alone; 9.86x beating O2 with 0 ABI change; 15.67x -> 1.20x O3-native with packed AVX1)
probes.estimated_loc: ~90 LOC Tier 1 (record loop-carry unboxing + multi-array hoist); ~120 LOC Tier 2 (F32 SIMD / packed local array)

probes.primary_mechanism: ANTI-OVERFITTING CATCH: Proven-18's .rodata LUT pass (Contract C) FAILED to fire on unseen $direct.crc_nib (16-case Nat match with case 0n: 0 and unsigned U32 values > 2^31), emitting a 15-branch linear cmp/jne chain (rodata=0, jcc=15) AND failing to inline $direct.crc_nib into $direct.crc_scan. 39.3M unpredictable branchy calls dominate runtime.

variants.name: a_rodata_lut_in_crc_nib
variants.note: 3.15x speedup (308.25ms -> 98.01ms) purely from lowering $direct.crc_nib to a 4-instruction .rodata RIP-relative table lookup (still out-of-line call).

variants.name: b_inline_rodata_lut_in_crc_scan
variants.note: 5.09x speedup (308.25ms -> 60.54ms, 1.020x vs gcc-10 -O3 -march=native — MATCHING C!) by inlining the .rodata LUT lookup directly into the hoisted $direct.crc_scan loop.

probes.general_compiler_pass: Generalize .rodata LUT lowering (Law C) to ALL dense Nat-match constant tables (including 0-valued arms, >=16 arms, and full 32-bit unsigned U32 constants up to 0xFFFFFFFF) + inline leaf .rodata LUT functions into hot loop callers.
probes.verdict: STRONG GO (5.09x speedup -> 1.020x O3-native, ~35 LOC general fix!)
probes.estimated_loc: ~35 LOC (fix .rodata LUT recognizer edge cases + inline leaf LUT)

probes.primary_mechanism: ANTI-OVERFITTING CATCH: Even though Proven-18 hoisted both Array<F32> handles in dot_row and inlined dot_row into matvec_rows, bend5k allocates F32 loop-carried accumulators in GP registers (%ebx) and loads F32 elements via GP mov + movd -> 4 GP<->XMM movd domain crossings per iteration, placing TWO movds directly on the 3-cycle addss critical path (stretching 3 cycles/iter to ~12 cycles/iter) + 98 spills in matvec_rows.

variants.name: a_xmm_resident_scalar_matvec_rows
variants.note: 3.78x speedup (165.29ms -> 43.76ms, BEATS gcc-10 -O2 at 0.990x and hits 1.090x O3-native!) purely from keeping F32 accumulator in %xmm0 (0 movd in loop) + direct movss mem loads.

variants.name: b_unroll4_xmm_strict_ieee_matvec_rows
variants.note: 3.77x speedup (43.82ms, 0.991x O2, 1.092x O3-native). Confirms Variant A already hits 95% of the Ivy Bridge 3-cycle strict IEEE-754 addss silicon floor (47.18M * 3 / 3.4GHz = 41.6ms).

probes.general_compiler_pass: XMM-Resident F32 Register Allocation Law: allocate F32 SSA values and loop-carried F32 accumulators in XMM registers with direct movss/mulss/addss memory operands (0 GP<->XMM movd inside FP loops).
probes.verdict: STRONG GO (3.78x speedup -> 0.990x O2, 1.090x O3-native from scalar XMM regalloc alone!)
probes.estimated_loc: ~70 LOC (XMM register class for F32 SSA values + direct movss load/store)

probes.benchmark: research/agy/bend5k/unseen_oracle_w19/u4_mergesort_list.bend (pure functional List<&2, U32> mergesort, N=8192 x 20 rounds)
probes.primary_mechanism: ANTI-OVERFITTING CATCH: Proven-18's TRMC pass (Law 5 / Contract I) only fires on simple single-list List.map/filter shapes and FAILED on 2-list multi-arm $direct.merge_go (1811 lines, 2 recursive $direct.merge_go calls, 101 spills, heap-allocating MCheck/MPick state wrappers and new Con cells on every comparison instead of relinking unique Con nodes).

variants.name: a_trmc_1pass_reuse_merge_go
variants.note: 3.27x speedup (112.48ms -> 34.43ms, 1.288x O2, 1.330x O3-native) via 1-pass multi-arm TRMC IMutField tail-pointer loop + in-place unique Con node reuse (0 recursion, 0 alloc).

probes.general_compiler_pass: Generalize TRMC (Law 5) to multi-arm / nested-match constructor-tail recursion (2-list merge) + transient state-ADT unboxing + unique Con node in-place IReuse (tail->tail = next).
probes.verdict: STRONG GO (3.27x speedup -> 1.330x O3-native; eliminates recursive stack & allocation)
probes.estimated_loc: ~85 LOC (multi-arm TRMC + unique Con reuse in tail-pointer loop)

already_beating_o3_native.u3_bytecode_vm: 0.86x vs gcc-10 -O3 -march=native (143.45ms vs 166.39ms) — confirms Proven-18 borrow + TSwitch jump-table laws genuinely generalize to unseen ADT interpreters.

top_new_general_laws_discovered: Law 7 (Dense .rodata LUT Completeness & Leaf Inlining): Fix .rodata LUT lowering when arm 0 returns 0, table size >= 16, or values > 2^31 (u6_crc32_lut: 5.09x -> 1.02x O3-native).

Law 8 (XMM-Resident F32 Loop Allocation): Keep F32 SSA values and loop-carried accumulators in XMM registers with 0 GP<->XMM movd inside hot loops (u5_matvec_f32: 3.78x -> 0.99x O2 / 1.09x O3-native; also accelerates u1_stencil2d).

Law 9 (Record Loop-Carry Unboxing + Multi-Array Hoist + F32 SIMD): Unbox single-constructor record state across self-TCO loops and hoist all unpacked Array<T> handles (u1_stencil2d: 6.17x scalar, 9.86x SSE4.1 64-bit slots, 15.67x packed AVX1).
Law 10 (Multi-Arm TRMC + Unique Con Reuse): Extend 1-pass TRMC IMutField to multi-arm nested matches like 2-list merge (u4_mergesort_list: 3.27x -> 1.33x O3-native).
